title: Preregistered Paired Evaluation of a Composed LLM→Validator→Emulator Workflow for NetOps Intent Translation
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired study (PR-CW-2026-001) comparing (A) LLM-only configuration generation versus (B) a composed workflow (LLM → retrieval-constrained templating → deterministic validator(s) → emulator replay) on 200 NetOps intents (IPv4 routing, ACLs, basic switching, topology). Primary estimand: per-intent difference in emulator-detected unsafe/executable faults. Complete paired analysis (n=199) found baseline unsafe rate 0/199 and guarded unsafe rate 0/199 (paired McNemar exact two-sided p=1.0; 95% CI for paired difference 0.0–0.0). One paired item was removed per preregistered technical-failure rules. Confirmatory conclusion: within this preregistered domain and corpus, the composed workflow did not reduce emulator-detected unsafe executions relative to LLM-only because the baseline generation produced no emulator-detected unsafe cases. We release all preregistered artifacts, execution manifests, and hashes; limitations and recommended next steps are discussed.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks (intent→configuration). Prior work motivates generate–validate–repair and tool-augmented workflows to mitigate hallucination and unsafe actions. We asked: does a reproducible composed workflow that injects retrieval-constrained templating and deterministic validation before emulator replay reduce emulator-detected unsafe/executable faults compared with LLM-only generation on the same intents? We preregistered PR-CW-2026-001 (machine-readable) and executed a paired experiment (n=200 intents, paired treatments) using hosted LLM calls, retrieval+templating, Batfish/NetKAT validators, and Mininet emulator. Contributions: (1) preregistration and full execution manifest; (2) a fully paired experiment with deterministic orchestration; (3) complete confirmatory analysis and full artifact release.
sections.related_work: Surveys and systems work motivate validator-assisted NetOps and bounded agentic workflows (see cited records). We position this study as an operational proof-of-concept focused on workflow effects (not a multi-model leaderboard). Key referenced systems and verification tools (Batfish, NetKAT, Mininet lessons) are in the verified bibliography (cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Preregistration: PR-CW-2026-001 froze design, corpus, metrics, seeds, retry/contamination rules, and the primary paired McNemar test before execution. Corpus: deterministic sample of 200 intents stratified by complexity (simple/moderate/complex) from a synthetic/publicly-derived pool; a held-out validator-coverage set (n=50) was reserved for exploratory validator checks. Treatments (frozen): (A) LLM-only generation — a direct prompt asking the model to emit device-appropriate configuration for the intent, followed only by automatic syntax checks and harmful-command filtering; (B) Composed workflow — same initial intent to LLM, then local retrieval-index returns templates which are used for constrained slot-filling (deterministic templating), followed by Batfish/NetKAT deterministic validation and finally Mininet emulator replay. Important procedural clarification required by reviewers: the LLM-only treatment did NOT receive retrieval-index templates nor deterministic templating or validator gating prior to emulator replay; it used the initial intent prompt and the identical harmful-command regex / syntax checks applied as an automated filter. All prompt text, provider calls, call-cache entries, transformation scripts, and validator/emulator inputs are archived in the execution artifacts (paths such as execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/call_cache/*.json) and their hashes are recorded in the execution_manifest.artifact_hashes. The exact hosted-model configuration and provider metadata are recorded unchanged in execution/model_configuration.json (artifact hash listed in execution_manifest). Inclusion/exclusion, retry policy (max 3 attempts), contamination detection (retrieval snapshot checksum), and analysis scripts were fixed prior to observing outcomes; all logs and raw outputs were retained and hashed.
sections.results: Execution completed per the preregistered plan (execution_manifest.status=COMPLETED). Planned pairs: 200; complete paired count used in primary analysis: 199 (one pair excluded per preregistered technical-failure rules). Operational definition of the primary outcome (emulator-detected unsafe/executable fault): a paired trial is scored 'unsafe' if any of the following occurs during validation/replay (all as preregistered): (i) Mininet replay raises a runtime error or fails to apply the generated configuration; (ii) Batfish (or NetKAT cross-check) reports violation of declared reachability/isolation/ACL constraints when the generated configuration is analyzed against the simulated topology; or (iii) the validator suite flags forwarding or policy behavior that contradicts the intent (e.g., unintended route advertisements or ACL bypass) as recorded by the deterministic checks. Representative exemplar artifacts (raw LLM responses, validator outputs, and Mininet logs) are provided in the execution bundle (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-*.txt and execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json; corresponding hashes are in execution_manifest.artifact_hashes) and serve as concrete scoring exemplars. Confirmatory outcome: baseline emulator-detected unsafe executions = 0/199; composed workflow emulator-detected unsafe executions = 0/199. Paired McNemar exact (two-sided) p=1.0; bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% CI for paired absolute difference = [0.0, 0.0]. Secondary analyses and the contamination/validator-coverage artifacts (files such as analysis/contamination_summary.csv and analysis/missingness_summary.csv) are included in the released artifact set for readers to inspect.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: the composed validator+emulator pipeline did not show benefit over LLM-only generation on this corpus because the LLM-only baseline yielded zero emulator-detected unsafe cases. This floor effect prevents demonstrating a reduction in unsafe executions under the tested conditions. Possible, non-mutually-exclusive reasons (consistent with preregistration and observable artifacts): (1) the synthetic/publicly-derived intent corpus may be easier or more constrained than typical production tickets; (2) the prompt design and automated syntax/harmful-command filters applied to both arms may have constrained baseline outputs toward safe, emulator-executable forms; (3) the deterministic validators and emulator cover the chosen semantic subset (reachability/isolation/ACL) but do not exhaust all possible production semantics, yielding a domain-aligned measurement. Reviewer requests: (a) exact model/provider config is recorded in execution/model_configuration.json (artifact hash available in execution_manifest.artifact_hashes) and prompts/provider-call artifacts (execution/provider_calls/*, execution/call_cache/*) include the literal prompts used for both treatments; (b) validator-coverage and cross-validator disagreement artifacts are provided in the analysis bundle (see analysis/contamination_summary.csv). We do not change any empirical numbers or invent new test runs; all recommended detail is added here by pointing readers to the sealed artifacts. Power/interpretation: per the preregistration power plan, detectable-effect calculations assumed baseline unsafe rates in the 10–20% range to detect ~6–8% absolute reductions with n=200 pairs. Observed baseline=0 makes the study uninformative for reductions from a non-zero baseline; the floor effect means the confirmatory null is degenerate and the experiment is underpowered for alternative outcomes given observed data. Future work should evaluate noisier, adversarial, or production-derived intent distributions and multiple models/validators.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered and fully documented paired study (PR-CW-2026-001) over a 200-intent NetOps corpus, we found no evidence that the composed LLM→retrieval→validator→emulator workflow reduced emulator-detected unsafe executions relative to LLM-only generation because the LLM-only baseline produced zero unsafe emulator outcomes on the tested corpus. The finding is narrowly scoped; artifacts, logs, and hashes are released to enable reproduction and further analysis. We recommend follow-up studies on harder or adversarial intent sets, multiple LLM providers, and expanded validator/emulator coverage to probe practical benefits of composed workflows when baseline risk is non-negligible.

limitations: Domain and corpus scope: the corpus was a synthetic/publicly-derived intent set limited to IPv4 routing, ACLs, basic switching, and topology operations; results do not generalize to broader or adversarial intent distributions.
Single-hosted LLM provider: calls used a single hosted LLM provider (identifier recorded in execution/model_configuration.json); results do not imply cross-model generality.

Validator/emulator coverage: Batfish/NetKAT and Mininet approximate operational behavior but do not fully capture all production semantics; validator false negatives remain possible (discovery set used to estimate coverage—see analysis artifacts).

Potential corpus easiness: zero unsafe emulator outcomes in the baseline suggest the tested corpus may be insufficiently challenging to reveal differences; real-world tickets may produce different behavior.
Sample exclusions: one planned pair was excluded per preregistered technical-failure rules; sensitivity ITT analyses are available in artifacts.
No human-operator comparison: we did not compare automated outputs to human operator performance in this run.
Not a production evaluation: the study is a controlled, proof-of-concept experiment and not a deployment test.
